clue.text: One VIP turning up to confront saint

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters climb the column and so read backwards

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a nob is a toff, a person of high rank
to face someone is to confront them

explanation.surface: An important person stands up to face down a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: I and NOB together are flipped to give BONI, and FACE is added: BONIFACE.
explanation.definitionFit: St Boniface was the English missionary who evangelised Germany in the eighth century.

clue.text: See 10 Across
Poet gets post but not a great deal

indicators.note: but not tells us to take the following small word away from what precedes it

blocks.note: post and mail are letters delivered
taken as written, then removed
a ton, as in 'tons of it', is a great deal

explanation.surface: A poet receives a letter, though not much of one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'not a great deal' as one phrase; the split falls after 'a', so 'not a' is a removal and 'great deal' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton was the seventeenth-century English poet who wrote Paradise Lost.

clue.text: Bar friend with a platitudinous style

blocks.note: to bar something is to ban it
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A pub's regular pal speaks only in clichés.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking banally means using trite commonplaces, which is the same as speaking in a platitudinous manner.

clue.text: Soldier with Eastern weapon within reach

indicators.note: within places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a span is the reach or extent of something
E is the abbreviation for East
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A soldier carries an oriental weapon that he can easily get hold of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reach' reads as a verb in the surface but is a noun meaning extent.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearman is a soldier armed with a spear, a standard infantry type of ancient armies.

clue.text: Job of gun dog being derided

blocks.note: first meaning: a retriever's task is to fetch the shot game ...
second meaning: an idiom for being booed or jeered by an audience

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally for the hunting dog and idiomatically for a performer who is hissed off stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the bird is a British idiom for being hissed or jeered, and a gun dog literally retrieves shot birds.

clue.text: Some of these Ravel rejected as a composer

indicators.note: some of says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them
something rejected is sent back, so the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone has thrown out some of Ravel's music in favour of another composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel looks like the composer in question, but he is only the hiding place; the answer is another French-born composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgard Varèse was a French-born American composer, a pioneer of electronic music.

clue.text: Nomadic drunk going round India or some island

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so these letters are jumbled
going round means the jumbled word surrounds the next letter

blocks.note: taken as written for jumbling
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A wandering drunk makes their way around India or some island.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of NOMADIC wrap around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominica is an island nation in the Caribbean's Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Sculptures of at least three Greek characters

blocks.note: one Greek letter, pi
two or more of the Greek letter eta, making at least three letters in all

explanation.surface: Statues bearing a few Greek letters as inscriptions.
explanation.walkthrough: One pi plus at least two etas makes 'at least three Greek characters'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, such as Michelangelo's in St Peter's.

clue.text: Dynamic individual that one should avoid contact with

definitions.text: that one should avoid contact with

blocks.note: first meaning: an energetic, lively person

blocks.clueFragment: that one should avoid contact with
blocks.note: second meaning: an electrified cable that is dangerous to touch

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue suggests a pushy person to keep away from; the second half is really a charged cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A live wire is idiomatically a vivacious person and literally a cable carrying current that can shock.

clue.text: Foody occasions – relations will eat each bit

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so one word swallows the others

blocks.note: ties are bonds or relations between people
EA is the standard abbreviation for each
a part is a bit of something

explanation.surface: At family get-togethers the relatives devour every morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests relatives at the table, but here it means bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea parties are social gatherings centred on tea, cakes and sandwiches, hence events about food.

clue.text: Great rift when cleric embraces heresy finally

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral
the final letter of heresy

explanation.surface: A deep split opens in the church when a clergyman finally adopts unorthodox views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great rift' suggests a schism in the church, but it is a physical valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep gorge, a huge cleft in the landscape, so literally a great rift.

clue.text: Your legs collapsed, climbing the stairs? That's unimaginable!

definitions.text: Your legs collapsed, climbing the stairs?

blocks.clueFragment: Your legs collapsed, climbing the stairs?
blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: someone with failing legs could not get up a flight of stairs
second meaning: the exclamation that something is too absurd to be invented

explanation.walkthrough: The first half pictures a literal failure to reach the top of the stairs; the second is the idiomatic cry about events stranger than fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase says reality is so absurd that no one could have invented it, i.e. beyond imagining.

clue.text: Mournful type's hit record

blocks.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
to enter details is to record them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit record' looks like a successful single; split it into two verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamenter is someone who laments, expressing grief, so a person given to mourning.

clue.text: Socialite and seductress ditching husband, a composer

indicators.note: ditching means dropping, so the following letter is thrown out

blocks.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society
a hussy is a brazen, flirtatious woman
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A society girl and a temptress have dumped a husband for a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was the French composer of Clair de Lune and La Mer.

clue.text: 'Relatively calm' perhaps is a label at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or tossed about, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written for jumbling
taken as written for jumbling

explanation.surface: A sea forecaster's phrase 'relatively calm' is described as just a label for conditions offshore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link word but its letters belong to the jumble too.
explanation.definitionFit: Water described as relatively calm is fit to be navigated by boat, one example of navigable conditions.

clue.text: A man involved in no branch of science

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
nay is an old word for no
a tom is a male, as in tomcat

explanation.surface: A man takes no part in any scientific field.
explanation.walkthrough: Nay is an old-fashioned or dialect word for no, and a tom is any male animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the branch of biology studying the structure of bodies.

clue.text: See 13
Reading University impeding a girl

indicators.note: impeding means getting in the way, so this letter stands in between the other two pieces

blocks.note: per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
Sal is a girl's name
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: In Reading, the university is getting in a young woman's way.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the English town with a university; it is the definition, the act of reading. 'a' is the setter's way of saying PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a reading through of something, a careful look at a text.

clue.text: Program location containing nothing suitable

indicators.note: containing means holding something inside, so the next letter is placed within

blocks.note: an app is a computer program
a site is a location
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A software package's website has nothing appropriate on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter O stands for nothing because it looks like a zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means apt or relevant, an exact synonym for suitable.

clue.text: Concert with huge pieces of publicity

blocks.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A concert comes with an enormous publicity campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous London summer series of classical concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Promos are promotional items such as trailers or adverts, i.e. publicity material.

clue.text: Stops and starts

blocks.note: first meaning: pauses or interruptions, as in a tea break
second meaning: begins, as when the day dawns or a story comes out

explanation.walkthrough: Stops and starts sounds like a single phrase for jerky motion; the two words are opposite meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A break is a pause in activity, while dawn or news that breaks is beginning, so the word covers both.

clue.text: Result of wearing bra creates a row

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: a bra lifts the bosom
second meaning: a noisy quarrel

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the hyphenated word as two separate words, chest raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust-up is a British informal word for a violent quarrel or argument, which is what a row is.

clue.text: Fellows having little energy and fevers on Scottish island

blocks.note: Coll is an island of the Inner Hebrides
E is the symbol for energy
an ague is a malarial fever with shivering

explanation.surface: Workmates are left listless and feverish on a Hebridean holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in an across clue puts the island first, before E and AGUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellows here means peers or associates, the people one works alongside.

clue.text: Release a bit of cricket equipment

blocks.note: first meaning: to free a suspect on payment of a security
second meaning: one of the two small crosspieces resting on top of the stumps

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket wickets are three stumps topped by two bails, which fall when the batsman is bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: To bail someone is to release them pending trial, and a bail is a crosspiece atop cricket stumps.

clue.text: See 6
American university's short tree or shrub

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter of the name is dropped

blocks.note: Cornell is an Ivy League university in Ithaca, New York

explanation.surface: A US campus has a stunted tree or bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornel is a dogwood of the genus Cornus, which grows as a small tree or shrub.

clue.text: Sign given by head of militia abandoning tanks

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so a letter is taken out of the word that follows
head of picks out only the first letter of the next word as what gets removed

blocks.note: the first letter of militia
fish tanks are aquariums

explanation.surface: A signal comes from the militia leader as he leaves the armoured vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanks' suggests military vehicles alongside militia, but these are fish tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquarius, the water carrier, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.
